purpose: The single shared Iranian mobile-number normalisation conformance corpus for the Alaa messaging providers. It began as the union of the two corpora that alaa-sms-provider-mediana and alaa-bale-provider built independently, preserving every input from both. It now also pins the display-separator rule the two providers settled on: whitespace, format and dash characters are matched by Unicode category rather than by an enumerated list, the solidus is stripped as a hand-typed separator, and the international prefix is removed only when the country code 98 follows it.
drift_rule: The two copies are byte-identical by design. A difference between them is a defect to report, not a local customisation to keep. Change both in one commit or change neither. A document that asserts the two channels agree is not evidence that they agree; only running both validators against this one file is.

channels.mediana: +989xxxxxxxxx - the Mediana/IPPanel Edge wire form, with the plus sign.
channels.bale: 989xxxxxxxxx - the Bale Safir wire form, the same digits with no plus sign.

null_means: The input must be rejected, with a non-zero exit and a stated reason, for both channels. It must never be rendered onto either wire.
canonicalization: One rule governs both copies of this file so they cannot drift apart again. On disk: json.dump(document, handle, ensure_ascii=True, indent=2) followed by a single trailing newline, so the file is pure ASCII, every non-ASCII character appears as a \uXXXX escape, and the bytes survive any platform, editor, or transfer path unchanged. Checksum: corpus_sha256 is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of json.dumps(cases, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':')).encode('utf-8') - that is, of the parsed cases re-serialised with the real characters in UTF-8 rather than with the on-disk escapes. The digest therefore describes the data and not one language's JSON escaping convention, so a Go, PHP, or JavaScript implementation can reproduce it without reimplementing Python's escaper. Case order is part of the hashed bytes and is fixed: accepted cases first (mediana_expected is not null), then rejected cases, and within each group ascending by Unicode code point of input. A merge that follows this order rebuilds the identical file. Reproduce the checksum from this file alone: python3 -c "import hashlib,json,sys; d=json.load(open(sys.argv[1],encoding='utf-8')); print(hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(d['cases'],ensure_ascii=False,sort_keys=True,separators=(',',':')).encode()).hexdigest())" phone-conformance-corpus.json

cases.note: Leading tab and trailing newline from a pasted value.
Canonical value with surrounding whitespace.
Parentheses around the operator prefix.
Parentheses around the operator code plus mixed spaces and hyphens.
Plus form with spaces.
E.164 with the plus sign. The form most third-party address books export.
International access code with spaces.
International access code 0098 standing in for the plus.
Vertical tab U+000B. Category Cc, so only str.isspace() catches it; an enumerated whitespace list that stopped at the tab, the newline and U+00A0 rejected it.

Spaces as display separators. This is the grouping the Alaa client shows on /login: src/i18n/fa/auth/login.ts:10 and src/i18n/en-US/auth/login.ts:10 both set the mobile placeholder to 0912 345 6789 with ASCII spaces U+0020.
ASCII hyphen-minus separators.
Full stops as separators.
Solidus separators. A person types this by hand, the ten digits stay unambiguous once the solidus is removed, so the solidus is stripped like any other separator.
Domestic trunk form. The most common form a user types into an Alaa form field.
Trailing zero-width no-break space U+FEFF, the byte-order mark.
Underscores as separators.
Next line U+0085. A C1 control that str.isspace() reports as whitespace, which is why the whitespace test is str.isspace() and not the Cc category.
Non-breaking space U+00A0.
Ogham space mark U+1680. Category Zs and outside the U+2000 block, so a list built from the U+2000 spaces alone misses it.
Figure space U+2007. Category Zs, and the space a digit-grouping display layer picks because it is exactly one digit wide.
Zero-width non-joiner U+200C inside the number.

ZWNJ U+200C inside the number. Persian keyboards emit it, it survives most copy-paste paths, and the Persian copy on the client's /login page carries it (src/i18n/fa/auth/login.ts:15 and :26), so a value pasted from that page can hold it.
Zero-width joiner U+200D inside the number.
En dash U+2013 used as a separator.
Em dash U+2014 used as a separator.
Line separator U+2028. The only member of category Zl, and one of the four inputs on which the two providers disagreed before the category rule replaced the list.
Paragraph separator U+2029. The only member of category Zp.
Narrow no-break space U+202F. Category Zs, and the space several locales use between digit groups.
Medium mathematical space U+205F. Category Zs.
U+206F NOMINAL DIGIT SHAPES, a deprecated format character. Category Cf, like ZWNJ, so a category rule removes it and an enumerated list does not.
Ideographic space U+3000. Category Zs, and one of the four inputs on which the two providers disagreed before the category rule replaced the list.
Fullwidth hyphen-minus U+FF0D. Category Pd and outside the U+2010 to U+2015 run, so the dash class is matched by category too.
Bare national significant number, no trunk zero and no country code.
Country code with no plus. Already Bale's wire form; Mediana still needs the plus added.
Non-breaking spaces U+00A0, which a plain str.strip() on space does not remove.
Arabic letter mark U+061C, a zero-width format character.
Arabic-Indic digits U+0660-U+0669. Same trap as the Persian-Indic case, different code block.
Arabic-Indic digits with no trunk zero.
Persian-Indic digits carrying the 0098 access code.
Persian-Indic and ASCII digits mixed in one string.
Persian-Indic digits U+06F0-U+06F9. Python str.isdigit() returns True for these, so a digit check that is not an explicit ASCII pattern accepts them.
Persian-Indic digits in the bare national form, so folding and prefix reduction must both run.
Leading zero-width space U+200B.
Zero-width space U+200B leading and BOM U+FEFF trailing.
Bidi marks LRM U+200E and RLM U+200F around the country code, as pasted from a right-to-left document.
Right-to-left and left-to-right marks around a spaced number.
U+202B/U+202C bidi embedding and pop, as emitted by a right-to-left editor wrapping a number.
U+202E/U+202D bidi overrides inside the number.
Empty string. There is no number to render.
Whitespace only. Distinct from empty: a naive truthiness check treats this as present.
Plus sign in front of the domestic trunk zero. The trunk zero occupies the position the country code belongs in, so this is not a number in international form.
Non-Iranian country code. Neither channel is provisioned for it.
A number outside Iran. This normaliser renders Iranian mobiles only.
Plus sign with no country code behind it. Removing the plus unconditionally would turn a malformed number into a well-formed one.
International prefix combined with the trunk zero.
The same landline in country-code form.
Non-mobile national prefix behind the country code.
An alphabetic sender label. A sender is never a recipient.
International access code 00 in front of the trunk zero, with no country code between them.
International access code 00 with no country code behind it. Removing the 00 unconditionally would accept a number that names no country.
Tehran landline. Valid Iranian number, not a mobile, so no messaging channel can deliver it.
Tehran landline. The national significant number does not start with 9.
National significant number starts with 8, which is not a mobile prefix.
Ten digits with a trunk zero: one digit short. Reject rather than pad.
Two numbers in one string. One input renders one recipient.
Two numbers separated by a solidus. Stripping the solidus concatenates them into an over-length string, which the length check refuses exactly as it refuses two numbers separated by a space.
Twelve characters: one digit longer than a national mobile number.
Twelve digits starting 09: one digit long.
A trailing letter. Letters are not separators and are not stripped.
National significant number starting with 8 rather than 9.
Eleven digits starting 98: one digit short on the country-code form.
Two numbers in one field. Stripping separators concatenates them into an over-length string; accepting it would send to a fabricated recipient.
Country code plus eleven digits: one digit too long.
Thirteen digits starting 98: one digit long on the country-code form.
Persian-Indic digits, one digit short. Folding must happen before the length check.
Devanagari digits. Only Persian-Indic and Arabic-Indic digits are folded.
Unicode whitespace only. Distinct from the ASCII whitespace-only case: nothing here is an ASCII space, and nothing survives cleanup.
Zero-width characters only. Nothing survives cleanup.
Zero-width characters only, which reduces to empty after stripping.
Superscript digits. Python's str.isdigit() accepts these, so a normaliser built on it would pass them.
